step: Block Visa (Tasreeh) — Employer Obtains Work Visa Authorization via Qiwa / MHRSD
authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) — Qiwa Platform
field_label: Block visa allocation approved on Qiwa; Nitaqat status green/platinum
non_obvious_official_guidance: The employer must hold a valid Nitaqat (Saudization) tier of at least 'Green' and apply through the Qiwa platform for a block visa allocation (tasreeh) before any individual work visa can be issued to an expatriate employee.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Employees cannot initiate a Saudi work visa independently — the entire authorization chain starts with the employer's Nitaqat compliance status. A yellow or red Nitaqat rating silently blocks all new visa issuances with no notification to the employee or applicant. Processing takes 4–12 weeks depending on quota availability. Companies below headcount thresholds for Saudi nationals may be unable to hire any new expatriates until they rebalance their workforce.
non_obvious_action_required: Before extending an offer to a foreign national, confirm the employer's current Nitaqat tier and remaining visa quota on Qiwa. If yellow or red, escalate to an MHRSD-registered PRO or legal adviser before proceeding. Factor 8–12 weeks for tasreeh approval into onboarding timelines.

step: Work Visa Application — Consular Stamping in Country of Residence
authority: Saudi Arabian Embassy / Consulate in employee's country of residence
source: Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Visa Portal

field_label: Medical fitness certificate issued at approved center in home country
deadline_label: Before work visa stamping; certificate valid ~3 months
non_obvious_official_guidance: Nationals from designated high-volume labor-sending countries (including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Indonesia, Egypt, and others) must undergo a medical examination at a GAMCA-approved center in their home country. The fitness certificate is a consular prerequisite for visa stamping.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The examination must be conducted at a specifically GAMCA-affiliated clinic — not any accredited clinic or hospital. Results are transmitted electronically directly to the Saudi government system; the individual does not carry the result. Certain findings (active TB, HIV, hepatitis B/C) result in automatic visa refusal with no appeal mechanism. Western-nationality employees may not face this as a hard consular requirement but will undergo an equivalent in-country test as part of Iqama processing.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the GAMCA appointment as the first action after tasreeh approval — slots at approved centers in major cities fill 2–3 weeks out. Verify the exact test panel required for the applicant's nationality and destination region. Do not proceed to visa stamping until the GAMCA certificate is in hand.

step: Entry on Work Visa — Saudi Port of Entry; 90-Day Iqama Clock Starts
authority: General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) — Saudi Ports of Entry
field_label: Work visa entry stamp; permitted-stay period noted
deadline_label: Day of arrival — 90-day Iqama deadline begins
non_obvious_official_guidance: A Saudi work visa is typically single-entry. The visa's validity window governs the travel-by date; once entered, the permitted stay is 90 days within which the Iqama must be obtained.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The 90-day Iqama deadline runs from the entry date stamped in the passport — not from the hire date, onboarding date, or the visa issue date. Overstaying the 90-day window before Iqama issuance triggers Absher-tracked daily fines (SAR 200/day) and can result in a travel ban and deportation order. The employer is jointly liable. This clock is tracked electronically and does not pause for weekends, public holidays, or Ramadan.
non_obvious_action_required: Record the exact entry date immediately and share it with the employer's PRO on arrival day. Do not allow relocation administration to proceed at a normal pace — the 90-day clock is hard and non-extendable in standard cases. The PRO should initiate the Iqama application within the first working week.
source: General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) — Entry Requirements

authority: General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) / Saudi Ports Health Authority
field_label: Biometrics captured; health screening cleared at port

step: In-Country Medical Fitness Examination — MHRSD-Approved Center
authority: MHRSD-Approved Medical Centers (Ministry of Health licensed)
field_label: Medical result transmitted to Jawazat; fitness confirmed for Iqama
deadline_label: Within first 2–3 weeks of arrival; required before Iqama issuance
non_obvious_official_guidance: An in-country medical examination at an MHRSD-approved health facility is mandatory as part of the Iqama application process, covering communicable diseases. Results are transmitted electronically to Jawazat.
non_obvious_actual_reality: This is a wholly distinct step from any pre-departure GAMCA examination — both are required and neither substitutes for the other. The in-country result is transmitted directly to Jawazat electronically; the employee does not carry it. A positive finding for a specified communicable disease triggers mandatory repatriation regardless of employer or employee circumstances. Appointment queues at approved centers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam can run 1–2 weeks during peak intake periods.
non_obvious_action_required: The employer's PRO should schedule the in-country medical in the first week of arrival as part of the Iqama initiation workflow. Do not wait for the employee to self-arrange — delays here push past the 90-day Iqama window.
source: MHRSD — Medical Examination Services for Expatriate Workers

step: Iqama (Residence Permit) Issuance — Employer Applies via Absher for Business / Jawazat
field_label: Iqama card issued; 10-digit Iqama number assigned
deadline_label: Within 90 days of entry (hard statutory deadline)
non_obvious_official_guidance: The employer's PRO must apply for the Iqama within 90 days of the employee's entry using the Absher for Business or Muqeem platforms. Prerequisite documents include: valid work visa entry, medical fitness clearance, passport-compliant photo, and valid CCHI health insurance policy.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The Iqama is the employee's primary legal identity document in Saudi Arabia — without it they cannot open a bank account, register a SIM, formally rent accommodation, or access virtually any government service. The employer (not the employee) is the legal applicant and bears liability for fines if Iqama is delayed. The employee cannot change address between arrival and Iqama issuance as the registered address on the application must match the actual residence. Exit from Saudi Arabia is restricted until Iqama is issued (exit visa required, controlled by employer on Absher).
non_obvious_action_required: Brief the employer's PRO on day 1. The employee must not change accommodation before Iqama issuance. Compile all required documents in the first week. Track the 90-day clock as a hard project deadline with weekly escalation if Iqama is not issued by day 75.
source: General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) — Iqama Services

step: Muqeem Registration — Expatriate Residency Tracking System
authority: Ministry of Interior / General Directorate of Passports — Muqeem Platform
field_label: Employee record active on Muqeem; employer linked
deadline_label: Upon or immediately after Iqama issuance

step: Absher Individual Account Activation — Digital Residency Gateway
authority: Saudi Arabia National Information Center / Ministry of Interior
field_label: Absher account activated; Iqama number and Saudi mobile linked
deadline_label: Within first week of Iqama issuance
non_obvious_official_guidance: All Iqama holders must register on the Absher Individual platform to access government services, manage residency, request exit/re-entry visas, and renew their Iqama.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Absher is not optional — it is the mandatory gateway to virtually every Saudi government digital service for residents. Without an active Absher account the employee cannot request exit or re-entry visas (required to leave Saudi Arabia and return), update their registered address, or initiate Iqama renewal when due. Critically, the account requires a Saudi-registered mobile number for OTP verification — meaning the employee must obtain a local SIM (which itself requires an Iqama) before Absher activation is possible. Exit from Saudi Arabia is employer-controlled via Absher: the employer grants or withholds the exit visa permission electronically.
non_obvious_action_required: Obtain a Saudi SIM card immediately after Iqama issuance — this is the prerequisite for Absher. Activate Absher within the first week. Notify the employee explicitly that their ability to leave Saudi Arabia (including for holidays or family emergencies) is controlled by the employer's Absher for Business permissions, not by the employee's Absher account alone.
source: Absher — Saudi e-Government Portal for Individuals

step: GOSI Registration — General Organization for Social Insurance (Occupational Hazard Branch)
form_name: GOSI Employee Enrollment — Occupational Hazard Branch
field_label: Employee registered on GOSI; employer contribution rate 2% of salary
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must register all expatriate employees with GOSI within 10 days of employment commencement. Expatriates are enrolled exclusively in the Occupational Hazard (OH) branch. The employer contributes 2% of the employee's salary; no employee-side deduction applies for expatriates.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Expatriates are NOT enrolled in the full GOSI Annuities (pension) branch — that is reserved for Saudi nationals. Expatriates receive only work-injury and occupational-disease coverage; there is no pension accrual, no unemployment benefit, and no end-of-service GOSI payout from this enrollment. Employees from countries with European-style social security expectations will find the coverage substantially thinner than expected. Saudi Arabia has no bilateral social security totalization treaty with most Western countries, meaning home-country contribution gaps may arise.
non_obvious_action_required: Clearly communicate to the employee that GOSI does not provide pension or unemployment coverage. Seek specialist advice if the employee's home country has any social security treaty with Saudi Arabia (rare). Review whether the employer's end-of-service gratuity obligations under Saudi Labor Law supplement or replace expected retirement contributions.
source: General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) — Expatriate Enrollment

step: Mandatory Health Insurance — CCHI Enrollment (Prerequisite for Iqama)
field_label: Employee enrolled; CCHI-compliant policy certificate issued
deadline_label: Before Iqama issuance — required as part of Iqama application
non_obvious_official_guidance: All employers in Saudi Arabia must provide CCHI-compliant health insurance to expatriate employees under the Cooperative Health Insurance Law. A valid CCHI policy is a prerequisite for Iqama issuance and renewal.
non_obvious_actual_reality: CCHI-compliant insurance must be issued by a licensed Saudi insurer on a CCHI-approved policy form — existing international or European corporate group health policies do NOT satisfy this requirement and will not be accepted by Jawazat. The CCHI minimum benefit level is relatively basic (Class C); employees accustomed to international private medical coverage will find significant gaps in specialist access, dental, and optical. Allowing the CCHI policy to lapse triggers automatic Iqama renewal refusal. The policy must be arranged before the employee travels if it is to be ready for the Iqama application.
non_obvious_action_required: Arrange CCHI-compliant coverage through a Saudi-licensed insurer before the employee departs their home country — waiting until after arrival adds pressure on the 90-day Iqama window. Explicitly verify with the insurer that the policy is CCHI-registered and accepted by Jawazat. Assess whether a top-up or international policy is needed to supplement CCHI minimums.
source: Council of Cooperative Health Insurance (CCHI) — Employer Obligations

authority: Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) — licensed commercial banks
field_label: Saudi bank account opened; IBAN issued
deadline_label: After Iqama issuance; required for salary payment

step: Ejar Rental Contract Registration — Ministry of Justice Platform
field_label: Rental contract registered on Ejar; Ejar certificate issued
non_obvious_official_guidance: All residential rental contracts in Saudi Arabia must be registered on the Ejar platform (Ministry of Justice). A registered Ejar contract is the legally recognised proof of residence.
non_obvious_actual_reality: An unregistered rental agreement has no legal standing in Saudi Arabia. Electricity connection (Saudi Electricity Company), water, and other utility applications require a valid Ejar-registered tenancy contract linked to the tenant's Iqama number. The Iqama address must match the Ejar-registered property. Landlords who refuse to register on Ejar are non-compliant with Ministry of Justice requirements. Some landlords — especially in informal housing markets — resist Ejar registration because it creates a traceable legal record; this is a risk signal.
non_obvious_action_required: Before signing any tenancy agreement, confirm the landlord will register the contract on Ejar. Require the Ejar certificate as a condition of move-in. Without it, utilities cannot be connected and the Iqama address cannot be formally validated. If a landlord refuses Ejar registration, treat it as a deal-breaker and seek alternative accommodation.
source: Ejar — Saudi Rental Registration Platform (Ministry of Justice)

step: Personal Income Tax — Nil Obligation (Saudi Arabia imposes no PIT on employment income)
field_label: Zero Saudi personal income tax on wages and salaries; no annual filing required
deadline_label: Ongoing — no Saudi filing obligation on employment income
non_obvious_official_guidance: Saudi Arabia levies no personal income tax on wages, salaries, or employment income for either Saudi nationals or expatriate employees. Zakat applies only to Saudi nationals on business and investment income and is not an employee obligation.
non_obvious_actual_reality: While Saudi Arabia imposes zero personal income tax on employment income, three non-obvious obligations remain: (1) The employee may remain tax-resident in their home country and retain filing obligations on Saudi-sourced income — this is not automatically extinguished by working abroad and depends entirely on home-country rules. (2) The employer pays an annual Expatriate Levy (linked to the Saned / Hafiz workforce development schemes) per expatriate worker — this is a cost to the employer, not deducted from the employee's gross salary, but it affects total employment cost modelling. (3) A 15% VAT applies to goods and services consumed in Saudi Arabia and will be charged on most purchases; it is a consumption tax, not an income tax, but materially affects cost of living.
non_obvious_action_required: Advise the employee to consult their home-country tax adviser to confirm whether continuing tax-residency obligations apply and whether a tax return must still be filed in their country of origin. Do not assume zero Saudi PIT equals zero global tax exposure. Reflect the Expatriate Levy cost in offer-letter total-cost-of-employment calculations.
source: Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA) — Individual Tax Information

step: Iqama Annual Renewal — Employer Obligation via Absher for Business
field_label: Iqama renewed annually; CCHI insurance confirmed valid
deadline_label: Before Iqama expiry (annual) — initiate 60 days prior
non_obvious_official_guidance: The Iqama must be renewed annually by the employer via Absher for Business or Muqeem. The renewal fee (Muqaabala) is paid by the employer. A valid CCHI health insurance policy must be in place at renewal; Jawazat checks the CCHI register electronically.
non_obvious_actual_reality: An expired Iqama creates immediate legal jeopardy — the employee cannot travel, transact with government offices, or prove lawful residency. Employers who allow Iqama to lapse face fines and the employee can be subject to detention. Processing takes 2–4 weeks and requires confirmed health insurance; initiating renewal 60 days before expiry is the safe practice. Exit/re-entry visa permissions (employer-controlled via Absher for Business) must also be reviewed at renewal — if not enabled, the employee cannot leave Saudi Arabia even temporarily.
non_obvious_action_required: HR must calendar every employee's Iqama expiry date and initiate renewal at the 60-day mark. Synchronise CCHI health insurance renewal with Iqama renewal to avoid a lapse that blocks the Iqama process. Verify and refresh exit/re-entry visa permissions on Absher for Business as part of each annual renewal cycle.
source: General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) — Iqama Renewal

form_name: GOSI Monthly Wage Report and Contribution Remittance
field_label: Monthly payroll submitted to GOSI; 2% employer contribution remitted
deadline_label: 10th of each month for the prior calendar month
